WebSearch and WebFetch (Tilburg research portal, PsyPost, aiweekly, UHD news, OUP PNAS Nexus page, arXiv abstract pages, ICML 2026 virtual site, Cornell news via search snippets)
coverage_limits: OpenAlex returned HTTP 429 (shared anonymous credit limit) after the first title passes, so all OpenAlex title+abstract passes failed; I replaced them with Europe PMC abstract and full-text searches and Crossref per-journal searches. Europe PMC does not index Humanities and Social Sciences Communications or Nature Machine Intelligence, and Crossref/OpenAlex lack most Springer Nature and Elsevier abstracts, so for HSSC and NMI coverage is title-level only. nature.com blocks scripted fetches, so designs and sample sizes for Nature-family papers without a PMC copy (e.g., Yuan & Peng 2026 Sci Rep; Corpus et al. 2026 NHB; the Lee & Chung 2025 NHB reply) are unconfirmed. Full-text searches (limited to PMC open-access content) surfaced experiments whose titles and abstracts do not name creativity (Wu et al. 2025; Melumad & Yun 2025), so similar hidden studies in non-PMC journals may remain. Deliberately excluded: non-generative AI studies with diversity or novelty outcomes (Choi et al. 2025 PNAS Nexus and Shin et al. 2023 PNAS on Go-playing AI), perception-of-AI-art studies, self-report surveys (many Sci Rep, PLOS ONE, HSSC SEM papers), model-only benchmarks (e.g., Ruan et al. 2026 Nat Commun LiveIdeaBench), and commentaries or news features (e.g., Traberg et al. 2026 Commun Psychol; Nature features on homogenization). Five off-lane records found along the way are included and flagged in evidence.

candidates.title: Introducing AI to an online petition platform changed outputs but not outcomes
candidates.task: petition writing on Change.org
candidates.evidence: Natural experiment: Change.org rolled out an in-platform 'write with AI' tool; a difference-in-differences analysis of 1.5 million petitions (plus repeat writers before and after) finds AI access altered lexical features and increased petition homogeneity without improving petition outcomes. Published in NHB on 2026-09-30; number of writers not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Experimental evidence of the effects of large language models versus web search on depth of learning
candidates.task: writing advice after learning about a topic via ChatGPT/LLM vs Google search
candidates.evidence: Seven experiments (n = 10,462) randomly assigned people to learn a topic from LLM syntheses or web links and then write advice themselves; advice written after LLM learning was sparser and less original, with higher pairwise topical (cosine) similarity and lower Levenshtein uniqueness across writers. Found only through full-text search; the abstract does not mention creativity.

candidates.title: Human-generative AI collaboration enhances task performance but undermines human’s intrinsic motivation
candidates.task: ChatGPT-assisted vs solo writing (Facebook post, performance review, email), then solo AUT and product-idea brainstorming
candidates.evidence: Four online experiments (total N = 3,562) randomly assigned people to collaborate with ChatGPT or work alone on Task 1, then all did Task 2 without AI, including an alternative uses test and brainstorming product-improvement and promotion ideas rated for quantity, novelty and usefulness. Full text reports no significant Collab-Solo vs Solo-Solo differences in solo idea novelty or usefulness in Studies 2-3; the abstract says Task 1 performance gains did not persist.

candidates.title: Cross-lingual effects of AI-generated content on human work
candidates.task: business emails addressing business issues (incl. product design, scientific discovery) in English, Arabic, Chinese
candidates.evidence: Study 2 is a randomized experiment in which 480 participants (160 per language) wrote business emails with or without AI-generated content; trained evaluators rated quality, and AI-content use was associated with less actionable and less creative output in Arabic and Chinese than in English.

candidates.title: AI models as cultural beings: Investigating AI cultural biases and the impact of cultural alignment on human–AI creative collaboration
candidates.task: business pitch ideas for local vs global tasks with ChatGPT or ErnieBot
candidates.evidence: Study 2 randomly assigned American and Chinese users to culturally aligned or misaligned AI models (ChatGPT vs ErnieBot; n = 385 in the analysis table) and had two evaluators rate pitch ideas on novelty and usefulness; alignment raised usefulness but not novelty for local tasks. A field study (n = 194 dyads) replicated; this is an AI-configuration comparison, not AI vs no AI.

candidates.title: Enhancing creative writing through AI-powered co-creation with cognitive and emotional outcomes
candidates.task: EFL creative writing instruction with ChatGPT-style writing assistant
candidates.evidence: 92 male intermediate EFL learners were randomly assigned (computer-generated) to high AI support, low AI support, or conventional instruction; posttest creative writing scored with a rubric covering originality and coherence improved most in the high-AI group. Whether the posttest was written with AI access is not clear from the text I read.

candidates.title: Generative AI as a cognitive support tool in early-stage design ideation: A human–AI co-ideation experiment
candidates.task: early-stage design ideation from a design brief (text-and-image AI workflow vs human-only brainstorming)
candidates.evidence: Counterbalanced within-subjects experiment with 32 design students; sequence allocation was balanced but not randomized. Three expert raters scored ideation outputs on six criteria: AI-assisted outputs scored higher on problem framing and mechanism, human-only outputs higher on innovation, with no robust differences on design attributes.

candidates.title: Individual skill differences and human AI interaction shape creative outcomes
candidates.task: AI-assisted creative task scored for novelty and usefulness by skill level
candidates.evidence: Uses quasi-experimental data to relate cognitive, informative and logical dimensions of human-AI interaction to the novelty and usefulness of creative outputs among low-, medium- and high-skill individuals. Sample size, task and whether a no-AI comparison exists are not stated in the abstract; no PMC full text was available.

candidates.title: iDesignGPT enhances conceptual design via large language model agentic workflows
candidates.task: conceptual engineering design challenges (e.g., GoAERO) with LLM agent workflows
candidates.evidence: Novelty, originality and diversity metrics are computed on system outputs versus GPT-4o and DeepSeek-r1 baselines; two user studies (n = 11; n = 37 novices split across human-only, GPT-4o, GPT-4o-CoT, DeepSeek-r1 and iDesignGPT workflows) mainly measured creativity-support and workload ratings. Included for recall; creativity of the humans' own outputs is not the main outcome.

candidates.title: ChatGPT-3.5 as writing assistance in students’ essays
candidates.task: student essay writing with vs without ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Nine students wrote essays with ChatGPT and nine without; grades, writing time and text authenticity did not favor the ChatGPT group, and similarity among essays was generally low. Essay quality rather than creativity is the main outcome; assignment method not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: The analysis of generative artificial intelligence technology for innovative thinking and strategies in animation teaching
candidates.task: 12-week animation course with generative AI tools vs conventional teaching
candidates.evidence: 120 students were split into experimental (GAI-supported) and control groups for 12 weeks with pre- and post-tests; reported gains are in learning outcomes, knowledge application and motivation, and creative expression is claimed but a rated creativity outcome is not clear from the abstract. Included for recall.

candidates.title: Enhancing heritage-oriented design learning through a value-sensitive approach to generative AI in higher education aesthetic pedagogy
candidates.task: heritage-oriented design (embroidery, ceramics) with a custom text-to-image/LoRA/ControlNet pipeline
candidates.evidence: 12-week quasi-experiment with 118 design students: the group using a value-sensitive generative AI pipeline outperformed a traditional-methods control on aesthetic appreciation, design implementation and cultural identity. Outcomes are design-learning measures rather than creativity scores; included for recall.

candidates.title: Enhancing art creation through AI-based generative adversarial networks in educational auxiliary system
candidates.task: student digital art creation with a GAN-based co-creation system vs traditional tools
candidates.evidence: Abstract reports that for 60 undergraduate art students the GAN system produced a 35.4 percent improvement in expert-judged creative output quality over traditional tools; the full text describes a student survey (n = 60) and an expert review (n = 12) of model outputs, so the design is unclear. GAN-based rather than LLM or diffusion tool; included for recall.

candidates.title: Reply to: ChatGPT decreases idea diversity in brainstorming
candidates.task: brainstorming with ChatGPT (reply in a Matters Arising exchange)
candidates.evidence: Authors' reply to the already-collected Matters Arising by Meincke, Nave and Terwiesch about idea diversity in the Lee and Chung (2024) ChatGPT experiments. No abstract is available and I could not read the text, so whether it adds new diversity analyses is unconfirmed.

candidates.title: Large language models are homogeneously creative
other_versions: arXiv 2501.19361 (We're Different, We're the Same: Creative Homogeneity Across LLMs)
candidates.task: AUT, Divergent Association Task, Forward Flow
candidates.evidence: Published version of an already-collected preprint. Responses from 102 Prolific participants and 22 LLMs on standardized creativity tasks show LLM responses resemble other LLMs' responses far more than humans resemble other humans (population-level response diversity).

candidates.title: Echoes in AI: Quantifying lack of plot diversity in LLM outputs
candidates.task: short story plot generation
candidates.evidence: Introduces the Sui Generis score and finds GPT-4 and LLaMA-3 story continuations reuse plot elements echoed across generations and across models, while plots of the original human-written stories (100 stories) are rarely recreated; human surprise judgments correlate moderately with the score.

candidates.title: Divergent creativity in humans and large language models
candidates.task: Divergent Association Task; haiku, story synopses, flash fiction
candidates.evidence: Compares semantic divergence of LLM outputs with a dataset of 100,000 humans on the DAT and creative-writing tasks: some LLMs exceed the average human but stay below the more creative half of humans; prompting strategies and temperature raise LLM semantic divergence.

candidates.title: Time-on-task and instructions help humans to keep up with AI: replication and extension of a comparison of creative performances
candidates.task: Alternate Uses Task and Remote Associates Task
candidates.evidence: Replicates Koivisto and Grassini's human-vs-chatbot AUT comparison with 100 humans (50 original instructions, 50 modified instructions and more time) against AI chatbot sessions; AI mean scores remained higher, but maximum scores did not differ under the modified AUT condition (semantic distance and human ratings).

candidates.title: Humans create more novelty than ChatGPT when asked to retell a story
candidates.authors: Breithaupt, Otenen, Wright, Kruschke, Li, Tan
candidates.task: serial story retelling
candidates.evidence: Compares three-step retelling chains by humans (348 retellers from a prior AMT study) and by ChatGPT accounts: humans create 55-60 percent novel words and concepts per retelling while ChatGPT changes little after the first summary; 531 Prolific raters scored emotions.

candidates.title: How funny is ChatGPT? A comparison of human- and A.I.-produced jokes
other_versions: doi 10.31234/osf.io/5yz8n (PsyArXiv preprint, as cited in Porter and Machery 2024)
candidates.task: humor production (joke prompts; satirical headlines)
candidates.evidence: ChatGPT-3.5 and laypeople (final N = 105) answered the same humor prompts, and ChatGPT wrote Onion-style headlines compared with published Onion headlines; separate raters (N = 200 and N = 217) judged funniness blind to source, and ChatGPT output was rated equally funny or funnier.

candidates.title: AI-generated poetry is indistinguishable from human-written poetry and is rated more favorably
candidates.task: poetry by ChatGPT vs well-known human poets, rated by non-experts
candidates.evidence: Two experiments (1,634 and 696 Prolific raters) found readers could not tell AI poems from poems by famous poets and rated AI poems higher on qualities such as rhythm and beauty. Mostly a perception study; included as an AI-vs-human creative-output comparison for recall.

candidates.title: I, ChatGPT: linguistic properties and human experiences of human- versus AI-generated stories
candidates.task: short fiction writing from similar prompts
candidates.evidence: Study 1 compares stories by ChatGPT and 100 student authors on linguistic properties; in Study 2, 380 readers randomly assigned to an AI or human story reported no difference in novelty or entertainment but less transportation for AI stories.

candidates.title: Rethinking literary creativity in the digital age: a comparative study of human versus AI playwriting
candidates.task: playwriting (one AI-generated play vs one human-authored play)
candidates.evidence: Computational and NLP analysis scores an AI-generated play and a human-authored play on originality, fluency, flexibility and effectiveness; the human play scores higher on all creativity indexes, with the AI play close on several.

candidates.title: Stylometric comparisons of human versus AI-generated creative writing
candidates.task: short stories from fixed narrative prompts (GPT-3.5, GPT-4, Llama 70b vs humans)
candidates.evidence: Burrows' Delta and clustering show human stories form broad, heterogeneous clusters while LLM stories are stylistically uniform and cluster tightly by model; number of human authors not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Experimental narratives: A comparison of human crowdsourced storytelling and AI storytelling
candidates.task: Pygmalion-themed short stories (crowdworkers 2019 vs GPT-3.5/GPT-4 2023)
candidates.evidence: Compares 250 crowdworker stories with 80 GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 stories written to identical prompts; AI narratives are more progressive on gender roles but offer less imaginative scenarios and rhetoric than human texts. Number of distinct crowdworkers not stated.

candidates.title: Comparative evaluation of OpenAI O1 and human performance in higher order cognition
candidates.task: benchmarks incl. creative thinking (originality) vs human norms
candidates.evidence: Compares o1-preview with human participant scores from established benchmarks across several domains; on creative thinking tasks the model's originality score (2.98) exceeded the human mean (1.74). Human data come from prior studies, so N is not a single sample.

candidates.title: A large-scale comparison of human-written versus ChatGPT-generated essays
candidates.task: argumentative student essays vs ChatGPT essays rated by teachers
candidates.evidence: Teachers rated ChatGPT essays higher in quality than student essays, and linguistic analysis (including MTLD lexical diversity) shows a distinct AI style. Argumentative rather than creative writing; included for recall as an AI-vs-human output comparison with a diversity-type measure.

candidates.title: Generative AI in academic writing: a comparison of human-authored and ChatGPT-generated research article titles
candidates.task: medical research article titles (300 human vs 300 ChatGPT)
candidates.evidence: Corpus comparison finds ChatGPT titles closely mirror human titles in length and form but show formulaicity and limited stylistic flexibility. Not a creative task; included for recall because it reports convergence and formulaicity.

candidates.title: When ChatGPT Writes Your Research Proposal: Scientific Creativity in the Age of Generative AI
candidates.task: brief research proposals (hypothesis, experiment design, justification)
candidates.evidence: Off-lane find (MDPI journal). Two blinded experts rated research proposals written by graduate students and generated by ChatGPT-4 for scientific creativity; ChatGPT scored higher overall and on originality and meaningfulness. Student N not stated in the abstract.

candidates.title: Quantifying large language model usage in scientific papers
other_versions: arXiv 2404.01268 (Mapping the Increasing Use of LLMs in Scientific Papers)
candidates.task: 1,121,912 arXiv, bioRxiv and Nature-portfolio papers, 2020-2024
candidates.evidence: Population-level word-frequency estimates of LLM-modified content rise over time (up to 22 percent in computer science); LLM modification is higher in papers from more crowded research areas, a link between LLM use and similarity among papers.

candidates.title: Writing without borders: AI and cross-cultural convergence in academic writing quality
candidates.task: over one million Web of Science social science abstracts, 2012-2024
candidates.evidence: Tracks readability-based writing complexity and LLM-associated adjectives and adverbs across countries; non-native English countries converge toward and overtake traditional leaders, and AI-assisted writing tools appear to contribute to this cross-cultural convergence.

candidates.title: Delving into LLM-assisted writing in biomedical publications through excess vocabulary
other_versions: arXiv 2406.07016 (Delving into ChatGPT usage in academic writing through excess vocabulary)
candidates.task: PubMed abstracts, excess vocabulary after ChatGPT
candidates.evidence: Published version of an already-collected preprint; excess style-word frequencies in biomedical abstracts give a lower bound on LLM-assisted writing. Usage-prevalence evidence rather than a direct diversity measure.

candidates.title: Scientific production in the era of large language models: Outcome-triggered treatment timing and spurious event-study dynamics
candidates.task: reanalysis of arXiv author productivity around first LLM-detected paper
candidates.evidence: Reanalysis of the already-collected Kusumegi et al. (Science 2025) study: using reconstructed arXiv data, placebo assignments and simulations, it shows that dating LLM adoption by the first detected paper mechanically produces spurious post-adoption productivity gains. Relevant to how the scientific-output evidence is weighed; productivity rather than diversity outcome.

candidates.title: Human direction drives creativity with large language models
candidates.task: brainstorming and writing with ChatGPT or Gemini; naturalistic chats
candidates.evidence: Off-lane find (PsyArXiv). Two controlled experiments with ChatGPT (N = 234; N = 205), a preregistered Gemini replication (N = 157) and 6,290 naturalistic chats show that people who direct rather than delegate (Creative Direction) produce more original content with LLMs, and higher direction reduces semantic similarity across people. Whether participants were randomized to AI vs no AI is not stated.

candidates.title: Incentives shape how humans co-create with generative AI
candidates.venue: ICML 2026 Workshop on Human-AI Co-Creativity: Advances, Opportunities, and Challenges
candidates.task: creative writing with interactive AI under originality vs quality incentives
candidates.evidence: Off-lane find (workshop paper). A pre-registered RCT among participants using AI interactively finds that rewarding originality rather than quality yields collectively more diverse writing, because those participants incorporate fewer AI suggestions verbatim. The randomized factor is the incentive, not AI access; N not on the page I read.

candidates.title: Generative AI Makes Creative Output More Homogeneous
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 2026 European Conference on Cognitive Ergonomics (ECCE 2026), pp. 198-201
other_versions: OSF preprint osf.io/rz5s4_v1 (Does generative AI make us think alike? A systematic review and meta-analysis of homogenisation effects in human-AI co-creation), per PsyPost report
candidates.task: meta-analysis of homogenization in human-AI co-creation
candidates.evidence: Off-lane find: the published short version (dated 2026-09-14) of an already-collected meta-analysis; 19 studies and 61 effect sizes give a small, significant homogenization effect of AI use (d = 0.334), robust to sensitivity analyses and publication-bias checks. First posting date of the OSF preprint not confirmed.

candidates.title: AI use in American newspapers is widespread, uneven, and rarely disclosed
candidates.venue: Proceedings of the 64th Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers), pp. 14554-14580
candidates.task: AI-generated text detection in US newspaper articles
candidates.evidence: Off-lane find: the ACL 2026 published version of an already-collected preprint on how widely AI is used in American newspapers. Reported only as a newer version; no diversity outcome confirmed.
